title: Atomistic Mechanisms of Hydrogen-Assisted Deformation and Nanovoid Formation in Polycrystalline Cu
content: Hydrogen (H) can degrade the mechanical response of polycrystalline Cu, yet the atomistic mechanisms linking grain-boundary H to void nucleation remain unclear. In this work, molecular dynamics simulations of uniaxial tension with an analytical Cu–H bond-order potential are used to study H-induced defect evolution in polycrystalline Cu. At the highest H concentration examined (20 mass parts per million), H localized at grain boundaries reduces the tensile stress by up to 0.3 GPa relative to H-free Cu. This response is accompanied by enhanced grain-boundary emission and accumulation of partial dislocations, reflected by an increased population of hexagonal close-packed (HCP)-coordinated atoms associated with stacking faults. H stabilizes free-volume regions at grain boundaries and triple junctions, promoting nanovoid formation near interfaces between face-centered cubic (FCC), HCP-like, and disordered environments. These results connect hydrogen-assisted plasticity with nanovoid stabilization in polycrystalline Cu and identify grain-boundary defect activity as a key mediator of H-induced mechanical degradation.
